Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 0.51% to 23,053 but decliners led 1,974 to 564
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +0.97% weighted by turnover, against -1.80% for the median stock, a gap of 2.8 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Dhanuka Agritech Limited rose 12.0% on 104 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Investor Presentation”.

Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited fell 6.3% on 126 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Link of Recording”.

Borosil Limited rose 20.0% on 102 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about fund raising, “Grant of employee stock options under "Borosil Limited - Employee Stock Option Scheme 2020"”.

Quick Heal Technologies Limited rose 12.9% on 294 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Flipkart looks to expand FPO tie-ups with focus on value-added, premium produce”.

Breaking
Banks report 10-50% gains in productivity, turnaround time and costs from AI-led initiatives
Kotak Mahindra Bank handled 20% to 30% higher corporate servicing volumes without adding headcount, while Axis Bank and peers report 10% to 50% turnaround gains from artificial intelligence deployments. Over time, these efficiencies lower operating expenses and contain cost-to-income ratios across private lenders facing persistent deposit cost pressures. March quarter operating expense growth will show whether these gains offset ongoing wage and technology inflation.

Asia shares bend under AI stress; Apple earnings loom
Asian equities fell as heavy capital expenditure guidance from major technology firms renewed return-on-investment concerns ahead of Apple earnings. Global technology sell-offs typically trigger foreign institutional outflows from emerging markets and compress valuation multiples for Indian software exporters like Infosys and Tata Consultancy Services. Upcoming management commentary on enterprise client budgets will indicate whether offshore discretionary technology spending is recovering.

Cyberattacks on banks, including AU Small Finance Bank, worry insurers as claim risks rise
AU Small Finance Bank is investigating a potential customer data breach involving a third-party platform, as rising attack frequency elevates claim risks across the banking sector. Regulatory penalties and remediation expenses pose downside risks to mid-tier bank operating margins. Listed general insurers such as ICICI Lombard will likely raise cyber underwriting premiums to protect loss ratios as claims multiply.

Flipkart looks to expand FPO tie-ups with focus on value-added, premium produce
Flipkart is expanding direct procurement partnerships with farmer producer organisations to source fresh produce for its quick-commerce supply chain. Bypassing traditional agricultural mandis lowers procurement costs and reduces inventory wastage, supporting unit economics in quick delivery. The expansion heightens competitive pressure on fresh grocery margins for listed platform operators Zomato and Swiggy.

PM Modi to meet Niti Aayog leadership on Nov 5; likely to review work as govt begins shaping FY28 Budget
Prime Minister Modi meets Niti Aayog leadership on November 5 to set early budget priorities focused on domestic manufacturing and job creation. Early fiscal planning signals continued capex commitment and potential expansion of Production-Linked Incentive schemes. This directly supports capital goods firms like Larsen & Toubro and industrial manufacturers. Final ministry allocation figures in December will confirm the policy emphasis.

India’s Data Centre Capacity May Hit 2 GW in 2026 as AI Demand Fuels Expansion - Dainik Jagran MP CG
Industry projections show India’s data centre capacity doubling to two gigawatts by 2026, driven by artificial intelligence workloads. This rapid buildout expands addressable markets for industrial electricals, power backup, and specialized cooling providers. Listed suppliers like ABB India, Cummins India, and Schneider Electric benefit from higher order intake. Grid connection timelines from state power utilities will verify actual commissionings.

Solar module manufacturers requested an extension to comply with mandatory domestic sourcing rules for input cells. Delaying local content rules allows module assemblers like Waaree Energies to preserve operating margins by continuing to import lower-cost Chinese cells. However, integrated cell manufacturers like Tata Power face slower volume growth. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy notification on ALMM implementation will confirm the final timeline.

KKR, Singtel, and Tata Communications put data centre operator STT GDC India up for sale at a valuation above 5.5 billion dollars. Bank of England poised to raise rates but may push back on bets for more
The Bank of England raised interest rates while signaling resistance to aggressive market expectations for further policy tightening. This UK monetary policy decision has negligible transmission to Indian equities, as UK macroeconomic shifts do not materially alter domestic rupee liquidity, corporate earnings, or primary Indian export demand.

India's 10-year bond yield may ease to 6.75-7% by March: SBI Research
SBI Research projects the benchmark 10-year sovereign yield will ease to 6.75% to 7.00% by March, driven by planned fiscal consolidation and reduced government borrowing. A decline in risk-free rates directly lowers wholesale funding costs for NBFCs and prevents treasury mark-to-market losses at state-owned banks. The central government's gross borrowing calendar in the upcoming Union Budget will confirm this trajectory.

This bilateral nuclear project between Turkey and South Korea has no direct transmission mechanism to Indian listed equities.

South Korea factory activity growth slows to 8-month low, PMI shows
South Korea's manufacturing PMI fell to an eight-month low, dragged down by softening global electronics demand and export orders. As an early bellwether for international trade, this slowdown points to weaker external demand for Indian specialty chemical producers and electronic manufacturing services firms. Next week's preliminary Indian merchandise export data will confirm whether this export drag is hitting domestic order books.
Reuters Business
COMMENTARY: India's booming growth has an earnings problem
Nifty aggregate earnings growth fell below 5% year-on-year last quarter, opening a sharp divergence from headline GDP growth above 7%. This disconnect compresses valuation multiples across consumer staples and automotive manufacturers, where urban consumption slowdowns restrict volume growth. Further cuts to full-year consensus earnings estimates during the upcoming quarterly reporting cycle will test foreign portfolio flows into expensive domestic equities.
Reuters Business
Reliance Industries eyes growth boost from O2C, retail and Jio businesses
Reliance Industries delivered second-quarter growth led by oil-to-chemicals, while retail EBITDA margins contracted under heavy digital commerce investments and Jio maintained double-digit revenue expansion. The drag on retail profitability moderates consolidated earnings quality, shifting near-term valuation support back toward cyclical refining and telecom average revenue per user growth. Retail square-footage productivity figures next quarter will indicate whether digital spending translates into cash flow.

Companies and earnings
Sun Pharma’s specialty portfolio, Organon deal to drive growth
Sun Pharmaceutical expanded September-quarter revenue behind domestic formulations and its global specialty segment, anchored by psoriasis therapy Ilumya and the Organon distribution partnership. Higher clinical trial outlays shaved operating margins, but rising specialty contribution reduces reliance on commoditized US generics, protecting aggregate return ratios. Specialty revenue run-rates next quarter will confirm whether organic prescription volume offsets elevated trial expenses.
ET Markets
Varun Beverages’ Q3 volume surge can’t mask margin pain
Varun Beverages grew third-quarter sales volumes by 28.7%, yet gross margins contracted because of elevated packaging costs. Operating leverage failed to offset input inflation, leaving net margins vulnerable unless the company pushes price increases or curtails trade promotions in rural channels. Polyethylene terephthalate resin spot prices over the winter quarter will confirm whether raw material pressure eases.

OPEC+ keeps December oil output targets steady ahead of tougher call for 2027
OPEC+ kept its December crude oil output targets unchanged, deferring planned production increases to counter slowing global demand. Steady supply keeps Brent crude rangebound, containing India's import bill and sheltering state-run oil marketing companies such as BPCL and IOCL from retail margin compression. Compliance data from overproducing members later this month will confirm actual seaborne crude availability.

Oil prices fall over 1% as Iran-Qatar talks raise hopes of diplomatic progress
Brent crude fell over 1% after Iran and Qatar opened talks to de-escalate Middle East hostilities. Easing oil prices supports the rupee and expands gross margins for paintmakers like Asian Paints, tyre manufacturers, and state-owned fuel retailers. A confirmed diplomatic framework or ceasefire announcement remains the key trigger to determine if this margin relief sustains.

Japanese investors deepen India bets, creating a bigger business opportunity for law firms
Japanese entities have signed 120 preliminary agreements targeting over ₹1 trillion in cross-border investments under Tokyo's ten-year, JPY 10 trillion pledge. These commitments direct foreign direct investment into domestic manufacturing, renewable power, and industrial infrastructure. That capital flow supports order books and project execution for engineering and capital goods firms like Larsen & Toubro through non-bank funding.
